summary: The core is built as a board-level circuit. A raster counter with phase strobes drives a time-multiplexed character-RAM fetch into 74LS166 shift registers, sprites go through a ping-pong pair of line buffers with 74LS161-style address counters, and the priority PROM is looked up per pixel. Collision is a set of OR-latches strobed by H-phase decodes. None of it follows MAME's per-frame draw_layers/draw_sprites/copy_layers loops, its precomputed draw_order table, or its bitmap-overlap collision tests. The only MAME-shaped piece is the Alpine Ski and Space Cruiser protection, which reproduces MAME's cracked lookup values.

findings.note: Every pixel, the priority PROM is addressed with {PRIORITY[3:0], SCN3, SCN2, SCN1, OBJ} (the per-layer transparency bits). Its 2-bit output selects which layer's colour index goes to the palette RAM address MA. MAME instead turns the PROM into a 4-entry draw_order list and copies whole layers in that order.

Each tilemap layer serializes three bitplanes through an ls166x3 shift-register model. The registers load on SNxLD, which compares the fine-scroll latch against HPIX[2:0], and clear on SNxOFF. This is how the board does sub-tile horizontal scroll, not as an offset applied to a tilemap.

HN[2:1] switches the character-RAM address between layers 3, objects, 1 and 2. Scroll registers are chosen by PH phase strobes and added to the H/V counter bits to address the tilemap and column-scroll RAMs. Results are latched on ~1HN. MAME pre-renders each layer to a bitmap with a loop over 0x400 offsets.

Two 256x4 line-buffer RAMs (U69/U41, m5501_ram) alternate on LNSL (V[0]). Each has a load/clear/increment address counter, the incoming pixel is merged with what is already stored using a zero check, and the readback register is cleared by OBJOFF. MAME has no counterpart to its per-sprite loop over 0x1f..0 with transpen and wraparound.

findings.signal: Object RAM scanned by H counter with adder Y-compare
findings.note: Object RAM is addressed directly by {OBJEX, HN[8:4], HN[2:1]}. Y is checked by an OD+V+1 adder whose carry-in is tied high (74LS83 behaviour), and the high nibble of the sum feeds INRANG. Attribute fields are latched on PH1/PH5/PH7 phase edges, as the board scans per sprite slot.

Hit registers OR in a one-hot of the HM sprite-slot bits. They are clocked by HLP0-2, which come from a 74LS139-style decode (U26), or by layer-pair NOR terms each pixel, and are cleared asynchronously by HTCLR. MAME instead runs bounding-box and bitmap-overlap tests per sprite pair and per sprite/layer after the frame.

The handshake, latch and address-counter logic is built as named 74LS74/374/191 flip-flops, latches and counters (UMCU_7A/7B/9/13/10/11) plus OR/AND gates. The core also implements the U18A 68INTAK toggle flip-flop on PC3 and gates Z80 INT with it. MAME's device leaves this out ('FIXME 68INTAK is on PC3 but we're ignoring it') and models the rest with scheduler callbacks.

Chip selects and nets use board-style names (CDR1RQ..CDR6RQ, OBJRQ, VCRRQ, SPH/SPV, SMD12, HTCLR, EPORT1/2, SOFF, U68B blanking gate). RAM instances carry board reference designators (U105_U104, U5756, U7273, U67). The 9th palette bit is captured in a separate U46A latch from an odd-address strobe.

The main-to-sound latch and its semaphores are edge-triggered flip-flops with async clears from the sound-side read/write decodes. The sound CPU's NMI is a gate expression combining those bits with AY3 IOB[0].

findings.signal: Protection values copied from MAME's crack
findings.note: On writes to D50F, the Alpine Ski protection uses MAME's exact case table (0x05->0x18, 0x07/0x0C/0x0F->0x00, 0x16->0x08, 0x1D->0x18, else data). The Space Cruiser D48B read is an XOR-0xFF toggle identical to spacecr_prot_r. Both are behavioural stand-ins, not board logic.
The D5xx/D4xx register addresses and the 8000-DFFF regions match MAME's map, as any correct implementation must.
